# CV Editor

> Free, static, client-only editor for one-page Harvard-style CVs and cover letters, with live PDF preview and a built-in ATS / "AI slop" check. No accounts, no backend: data stays in the user's browser.

This file tells AI assistants and agents how to create or edit a CV in this app for a user.
The app never calls an AI itself. You (the assistant) write the content; the app renders, checks and exports it.

## Agent Skill (best if your environment supports skills)

[cv-editor-skill.zip](https://cv-editor.fynx.io.vn/cv-editor-skill.zip) unpacks to a `cv-editor/` skill folder: SKILL.md, the writing rules, the schema, and `scripts/cv_tool.py` (decode a `#cv=` link, check a CV for ATS and AI-slop problems, build the hand-off link). Claude Code: unzip into `~/.claude/skills/`. Claude apps: Settings > Capabilities > Skills. Any agent with a shell can also just download it and run the script.

## Files for you

- [Writing rules](https://cv-editor.fynx.io.vn/ai/cv-writing-rules.md): how to write the content (no invented facts, no slop, Harvard layout). Read before writing.
- [JSON Schema](https://cv-editor.fynx.io.vn/ai/schema.json): the exact payload shape.
- [Example payload](https://cv-editor.fynx.io.vn/sample.json): a complete real CV in that shape.

## Workflow

1. Get the facts from the user: target role and job description, each job (what was broken, what they did, tools, measurable result), projects, education. Ask in small batches. Never invent numbers, tools, employers or dates.
2. Write the CV following the writing rules.
3. Hand it to the user with ONE of the methods below.
4. Tell the user to open the "Check" panel in the app: it flags ATS and AI-slop issues (uniform "Label:" bullets, buzzwords, skills claimed but never shown, page count, JD terms missing). Fix what it finds.

## Hand-off methods

### A. Link (best for chat assistants)

Give the user a link that opens the app with the CV loaded. The payload lives in the URL fragment (after `#`), which browsers never send to the server.

- If you can run code, build a compact link: raw-deflate the UTF-8 JSON, base64url it, and prefix `z:`.

```python
import json, zlib, base64
data = {...}  # the payload
raw = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
c = zlib.compressobj(9, zlib.DEFLATED, -15)  # wbits=-15 means raw deflate
packed = c.compress(raw) + c.flush()
print("https://cv-editor.fynx.io.vn/#cv=z:" + base64.urlsafe_b64encode(packed).decode().rstrip("="))
```

- Without compression: `#cv=b64:` + base64url(UTF-8 JSON).
- Without code: `#cv=` + encodeURIComponent(minified JSON). Long, but works.
- Add `&mode=merge` at the very end to apply the payload as a patch instead of replacing the whole CV.
- If the JSON is hosted somewhere public over https (for example a raw GitHub gist), use `#cv-src=<url-encoded https URL>`.

The user can undo an imported link with one click.

### B. Paste (always works)

Output the payload in one fenced json code block. The user copies it and presses Ctrl+V anywhere on the app page (outside a text field). The app detects CV JSON and imports it. A .json file can also be dropped onto the page.

### C. Browser agents

If you control a browser, open https://cv-editor.fynx.io.vn/ and use the JavaScript API instead of filling forms:

```js
await new Promise(r => { const t = setInterval(() => window.cvEditor && (clearInterval(t), r()), 100) })
cvEditor.load(payload)          // replace the whole CV (object or JSON string)
cvEditor.patch({ cv: { objective: "..." } })   // partial update
cvEditor.audit("<job description text>")       // { score, findings[], stats } ATS + slop check
cvEditor.pageCount()            // aim for 1; re-read ~1s after a change
cvEditor.downloadPdf()          // or: await cvEditor.pdfBase64()
await cvEditor.shareLink()      // compact link that reproduces this CV
cvEditor.undo()                 // revert the last load/patch
cvEditor.getState()             // current full state
```

## Payload essentials

- Top level: `cv` (content), `coverLetter` (optional), and optional layout keys: `template` ("harvard" | "modern"), `language`, `sectionsOrder`, `disabledSections`.
- Bullets are objects: `{ "id": "short-unique", "type": "l1", "text": "..." }`. `type` is `l1` | `l2` | `l3` | `header`. Text supports `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `<u>underline</u>`.
- Enable either `objective` or `summary`, not both: put the other in `disabledSections`.
- In `mode=merge` / `patch`, any `cv` field you send replaces the current value entirely (arrays are replaced, not merged).
- Dates: one format everywhere, e.g. `07/2025 - Present`.
